title: Pokémon Fans Take Over San Francisco
summary:
Imagine a street where giant Pokémon stand tall, music plays, and 50,000 fans cheer. That's what happened in August at the Pokémon World Championships in San Francisco. Kid Reporter Adam Sadi was there, and he says it was amazing.

Inside the Moscone Center, players battled with video games and cards. Some were kids who had practiced for years. Adam met Haruki Okunishi, a top junior champion from Malaysia. Haruki's secret? "I just practice and practice!" he said. Some matches last an hour, but Haruki says it's still a lot of fun.

Outside, fans dressed as Pokémon characters. One fan came as Umbreon and drove seven hours to get there! Another, dressed as Absol, said Pokémon "brings together people of all backgrounds and all ages."

But the coolest part? Adam saw two real-life motorcycle Pokémon: Honda Koraidon and Toyota Miraidon. They are full-size and futuristic. Koraidon even blinked at him!

Pokémon is 30 years old, but at Worlds, it felt brand new. As Adam put it, the world behind the cards and screens suddenly felt alive and huge.
why_it_matters: It shows how a hobby you love can grow into a huge community where people of every age and background share something fun.

background_read: Pokémon started in Japan as a video game in the 1990s and grew into one of the biggest entertainment brands in the world, with games, trading cards, cartoons and movies.
The Pokémon World Championships is a yearly event where the best players from many countries meet to battle with video games and cards.
San Francisco (a big city in California, USA) is where the event was held, inside the Moscone Center, a huge building used for big gatherings.
Honda and Toyota are two large Japanese companies that built life-size Pokémon able to move like real motorcycles, which is why fans could see them out on the street.
Article_Structure: WHO: About 50,000 fans, players like junior champion Haruki Okunishi from Malaysia, and Kid Reporter Adam Sadi.
WHAT: Fans and players gathered for the Pokémon World Championships, with video game and card battles, costumes, and two life-size motorcycle Pokémon.
WHERE: At the Moscone Center in San Francisco, in the United States.
WHY: It shows how Pokémon brings together people of all backgrounds and ages, and how a 30-year-old game can still feel brand new.

perspectives.description: They love having a place where thousands of people who enjoy the same thing can meet and cheer together.
They use the event to show off clever machines that look like Pokémon, which makes the games feel real.
Some may say big events like this are mostly about selling cards, games and toys to fans.
